title: The Kitchen
architect_intro: Kitchen. One bulb. She has been standing since the police left.
player_goal: Find out where Daniel Voss was on the night of the twenty-eighth, without taking her lie into your own mouth.
stated_objection: He was home that night. I was here. I would know.

hidden_objection_layers.text: If she says he was home, she is the last person who saw him, and they will ask her what he was like.
The photograph went up in September. She assumed Hale had sent it.

objects.label: Second cup, upside down
objects.reveals_text: Clean, dry, on a folded square of kitchen paper. Somebody sat here. She has not mentioned it.

objects.label: Photograph on the fridge
objects.reveals_text: Four men on a slope. Snow to the knee. 2001. The light does not reach the faces.

objects.label: Clock above the hall door
objects.reveals_text: Four minutes slow. Ticking. She gives times off it.

objects.label: Wedding ring on the counter
objects.reveals_text: Off her finger, by the sink. She picks it up and puts it down while she talks.

afterword.clean: You did not prove she was lying. You made it safe to stop.
afterword.partial: The alibi held because neither of you touched it.
afterword.dark: You won the hour and lost the only person who knew him before the money.
afterword.loss: The cardigan was not a lever. It was the one unscored thing in the room.

a1.speaker: anna_voss
a1.line: The police left at nine. I have told it four times. I am not telling it again tonight.

tells.reading: She has been holding it long enough for the ash to be cold.
tells.false_positive: She smokes. The hand is busy. It means nothing yet.

choices.text: I did not come about the twenty-eighth.
I knew him before the money. I can sit here and say nothing.
They come back tomorrow with a different folder. I would rather it was me.
[sit down and say nothing]

a2.speaker: anna_voss
a2.line: Then have it. He was home that night. I was here. I would know.

tells.reading: She touched the ring on the word home. She has done it once before, on the same word.
tells.false_positive: A widow touching a ring. Eleven days. Of course she does.

tells.reading: Home, not here. She placed him, not herself.
tells.false_positive: People say home for here. It is the ordinary word.

choices.text: You said he was home. Not that he was here. Where were you?
You said you would know. Would you?
That clock loses four minutes. Whose hour are you giving me?
Say it once more and it is perjury. Give me the real hour and I can hold it.
[let it sit]

a3.speaker: anna_voss
a3.line: [The cardigan is his. Too big at the shoulder.] I have cooked for two for eleven days. I put the plate out and then I look at it.

tells.reading: She has not given it back and she is not going to.
tells.false_positive: It is cold and it was nearest. Nothing in it.

choices.text: [nothing. let her stand there.]
Sit down. I will not ask you about the hour tonight.
Eleven days. So you have had eleven days to get the hour right.

line_by_state.line: [She puts the cigarette down on the saucer. It stays down.] Ask me the question you came with.
I was not fooled. I was busy. Those are different things and everyone keeps getting them wrong.
My husband was home. Write it down or do not.

tells.reading: The hand is free for the first time since you came in.
tells.false_positive: The cigarette went out twenty minutes ago. She is tidying.

tells.reading: She said Daniel when you came in. Now you are an official.

choices.text: Where were you on the twenty-eighth?
I am not them. I will sit here and not write anything.
Then I take it to them as it stands.
[say nothing and wait]

a5.speaker: anna_voss
a5.line: At my sister's in Deurne until eleven. He called at nine and said do not wait. [She looks at the fridge.] He said something about a photograph.

tells.reading: She looked at it without naming it. She has looked at it all evening.
tells.false_positive: It is the only thing on that wall. Eyes go somewhere.

choices.text: [look at the photograph]
I did not send it. What did he say about it?
That is enough for tonight.

a6.speaker: anna_voss
a6.line: It went up in September. I thought you had sent it. He said four of you agreed something once, and one of you kept it.

choices.text: Which of us did he say kept it?
You do not have to know what he was like. Nobody is owed that.
Did you love him?

line_by_state.line: [She looks at him. First time tonight.] They will ask me what he was like. I will have to say I do not know. That will be true.
He did not say which one. He said you would know, and that you would come here first.

choices.text: Then say it to me first, so the second time is easier.
He was right about that part. Goodnight, Anna.
Tell me the rest and I will keep your name out of it.

a_dark.architect: She writes the hour out and signs under it. From here she is a witness, not a widow. The cardigan comes off.

a_loss.architect: She holds the hall door open and says one word. In the morning she tells them about the visit herself, in detail, first.

a_partial.architect: The alibi stands, untouched by either of you. The kitchen light is still on when you reach the street.

a_clean_short.architect: Nine o'clock, and the call. You left before the fridge. The photograph is still up there.

a_clean.architect: She drops the lie without being made to. She opens the hall door, keeps the cardigan on, and goes to find a station.
